questions.q: Match each part of Kafka Connect to its job.
pairs: Describes the data and splits the job into tasks
Copies the data, run by a worker
Converts between Connect's data format and the bytes written to Kafka
Changes single messages, or drops them with Filter and a predicate
questions.explain: A connector does no copying itself: it splits the job into source or sink tasks that workers run. Converters, set on the worker and optionally per connector, turn Connect's data into bytes and back, so any connector works with any format. Single message transformations change records in flight, and can be applied conditionally with predicates.

questions.q: A sink connector's task has failed. Put the steps to bring it back in order, first to last.
items: Read GET /connectors/{name}/status to find the failed task and its error
Fix the cause of the error
Check GET /connectors/{name}/status again until the task is RUNNING
questions.explain: Connect does not restart failed tasks automatically; restart them through the REST API. The status endpoint reports each connector's and task's state, worker and errors, so it is where you start and where you confirm the fix.
